#### First steps

Our learning happens from the first moments of life, with new knowledge built upon the previous ones.

Let's look at this in more detail in this lesson.

As babies, we are introduced to toys that give us fun, but they are also the foundation for our future.

Let's look at a toy that has several dolls placed one inside another: the Matryoshka (матрёшка).

#### The stages

Doctor Francisco A. González Redondo has a proposal that fits perfectly with the Matryoshka (матрёшка) doll.

Our first years at school would be a pre-science phase, in which we get to know some ideas.

In the second phase of student life, we have a scent, an initial taste, which would be the proto-science phase.

Finally, when we reach college, we come into contact with deeper knowledge and get to know science.
Can we represent the stages of learning (pre-sciences, proto-sciences, and sciences) with the Matryoshka (матрёшка) doll?

#### Playing and living

The dolls shown at the beginning of the lesson, with which some children play when they are little, are connected to our learning.

The smallest doll is the pre-science phase, in which we learn letters, numbers, and what a day is.

The second doll, which has the smallest one inside it, is the proto-science phase, in which we learn to describe life with texts, to represent what we see with formulas, and we see that a day is more than the time in which we see the sun.

The third doll has the other two inside it and is the science stage. In it, we learn the origin of words, the foundation for formulas, and that we are all star dust.

And, since knowledge never stops, the fourth, the fifth, and other upper dolls are added as we learn more and more.

#### Conclusion

In this lesson, we learned that knowledge is built in layers, like a toy that children play with when they are little.

In addition, we saw that the knowledge we have since childhood helps us with future knowledge.

In the next lesson, we will learn how each person learns.
